images.filename: Four People Beside Markers on the Little Bighorn Battlefield (141cd02b47be4d26a866beb15a95f3a7).tif
images.caption:
LIBI_00312_11193; Albumen cabinet photo. This image depicts view of four people standing beside markers on the battlefield. Left to right they are identified as:  Peter Thompson; Mrs. Missouri Ann Wycoff;  Sergeant Daniel Knipe from Company C of the 7th U. S. Cavalry; and Curly, the Crow Scout.  Mrs. Missouri Ann Wycoff Bobo, the wife of Sergeant Lemuel Edwin Bobo. Sergeant Bobo served  in Company C of the U.S. 7th Cavalry. He died during the Battle of Little Bighorn. She later married Daniel Knipe. This image was produced by an unknown photographer, in August of 1909. ; album, photograph;Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00312_11193, Unknown Photographer, "Four People Beside Markers on the Little Bighorn Battlefield," August 1909.

images.filename: Group on Horseback with a Running Buffalo in the Foreground, During a Hunting Party for Lord Waterpark Hosted By George (225b81a1f8314b84b46d9f5d1a97b1e9).tif
images.caption:
LIBI_00019_00499; This item is an original albumen, card-mounted photograph of a group on horseback, with a running buffalo in the foreground, during a hunting party provided to Lord Waterpark by George A. Custer.  The photograph is 4 1/4 x 6 1/4" (8" x 9 7/8" mounted).  As noted on page 85 of D. Mark Katz's book, the image was produced in 1869 by W.J. Phillips of Preston, Missouri.  Some fading and water stains are evident on the image.  Katz identifies the subjects, from left to right, as: an orderly, Lieutenant Henry J. Nowlan, Sutler Hill P. Wilson, Captain Thomas Weir, Lieutenant James M. Bell, Lieutenant Francis M. Gibson, Lieutenant Colonel George A. Custer, Captain Frederick Benteen, Lieutenant Thomas W. Custer, Captain William Thompson and Charley Thompson.  On the front, a handwritten notation reads, "Same size. Send us the wood before cutting."  On the verso, a handwritten notation reads, "Buffalo near Ft. Hays."Note: "Pkg #12" and "Box 5" handwritten on the verso.Photograph reprinted in "The C

images.filename: Bloody Knife, General George Armstrong Custer, Private John Noonan and Colonel William Ludlow with a Bear Killed While Hunting (32f3eb447a014d32b3fb076b0bc1fdc4).tif
images.caption:
LIBI_00019_00488; This item is an original albumen photograph of a hunting party and large bear killed on the Black Hills Expedition.  The photograph is 6 1/2 x 9 1/8" (8 x 9 1/2" mounted) and was produced in circa 1874 by William H. Illingworth of St. Paul, Minnesota.  On the front, a handwritten notation reads, "Gen'l Custer in [illegible word] with his first grizzly [illegible words]."  On the verso, a handwritten notation in pencil reads, "Col. Ludlow/Private Noonan/Bloody Knife - Indian Scout" and is signed by Elizabeth B. Custer.  General George A. Custer is seated between Bloody Knife and Private Noonan, directly behind the bear.  A letter recounting the killing of the bear is reprinted in Mrs. Custer's book, "Boots and Saddles," page 304.; Print, Photographic [Mounted on Card]; Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00019_00488, W. H. Illingworth, "Bloody Knife, General George Armstrong Custer, Private John Noonan and Colonel William Ludlow with a Bear
Keywords: little bighorn battlefield national monument

images.filename: Group Mounted on Horseback Along Reno's Crossing (5554fae3efb641b585d59852cf46e67d).tif
images.caption:
LIBI_00019_00573; This item is an original albumen, card-mounted photograph of a group on horseback at the crossing where Major Marcus Reno escaped during the Battle of Little Big Horn.  The imperial view photograph is 6 1/2 x 9" (6 7/8 x 9 7/8" mounted) and was produced in 1886 by David F. Barry at the 10th anniversary of the battle.  On the front, a typed notation in gold ink reads, "Reno Crossing, Custer Battlefield, June 26, 1886."  On the verso, a handwritten notation in pencil reads, "Custer Battle Field June 25th 1886."  Handwritten description provided by Elizabeth B. Custer.  The photographer's stamp is printed in brown ink.; Print, Photographic [Mounted on Card]; Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00019_00573, D. F. Barry, "Group Mounted on Horseback Along Reno's Crossing," June 26, 1886

images.filename: High Angle View of the National Cemetery (1bb2117b-a462-4d64-9c0f-b4711c75d4d6).jpg
images.caption:
A high angle perspective of a cemetery includes a flagpole at center in a conifer tree-lined walkway, neat rows of marble grave markers and burial sections, a Superintendent's House in the rear, and parking lot to the right. Rolling open grasslands extend in the distance.
A high angle perspective emphasizes the design characteristics of the historic landscape, with the flagpole, tree-lined walkways, neat rows of marble grave markers and burial sections, and Superintendent's House in the rear (at the original entrance). The cemetery landscape continues to be a place of solemn commemoration, and it also is a reflection of efforts to formalize memorialization on the battlefield and in the country.
Keywords: cemetery; national cemetery; designed landscape; aerial; flagpole; Little Bighorn Battlefield
